gloss: to meddle; to interfere; to butt in; to stick one's nose into

definitions.gloss: to meddle; to interfere; to butt in; to stick one's nose into
definitions.explanation: to meddle; to interfere; to butt in; to stick one's nose into

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}のことに{口出|くちだ}しするな。
examples.english: Don't meddle in other people's business.

examples.japanese: {親|おや}はいつも{子|こ}どもの{交友|こうゆう}{関係|かんけい}に{口出|くちだ}しする。
examples.english: Parents always meddle in their children's friendships.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}が{細|こま}かいことまで{口出|くちだ}ししてくるので、やりにくい。
examples.english: My boss interferes with every little detail, which makes it hard to work.

examples.japanese: {余計|よけい}な{口出|くちだ}しはしないでほしい。
examples.english: I wish you wouldn't butt in with unnecessary comments.

notes:
Describes uninvited interference in someone else's affairs or decisions. Almost always carries a negative nuance — the speaker views the intervention as unwelcome or overstepping boundaries. Composed of {口|くち} (mouth) + {出|だ}す (to put out).

USAGE:
- Often used with に to mark what is being meddled in: {人|ひと}のことに{口出|くちだ}しする
- The noun form {口出|くちだ}し is also common: {余計|よけい}な{口出|くちだ}し (unnecessary meddling)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {余計|よけい}な{口出|くちだ}し: unnecessary meddling
- {口出|くちだ}しするな: don't interfere
- いちいち{口出|くちだ}しする: meddle in every little thing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {干渉|かんしょう}する: to interfere — a more formal term, often used in political or institutional contexts
- おせっかいを{焼|や}く: to be nosy; to be a busybody — focuses on offering unwanted help or advice
- {首|くび}を{突|つ}っ{込|こ}む: to stick one's nose into — a more colloquial, vivid expression for meddling
